entry.value: The Initial Franchise Fee (amount blank in the Declarations Page) is payable in full on the day the franchisee signs this Agreement, or a portion then with the remainder plus interest under the 60-month Promissory Note (Exhibit I). The Royalty Fee is (a) the greater of 20% of Gross Revenues on policies in their initial term or the monthly Minimum Royalty, $600 for months 6 to 18 after the Commencement Date and $1,000 for the remainder of the term, and (b) 50% of Gross Revenues on renewal and re-write policies. The Marketing Contribution is up to 2% of Gross Revenues each Month, and a majority of the region's Goosehead Business owners may increase Regional Fund contributions by up to an additional 2%. A Technology Fee reimburses the franchisor's cost of providing Required Software and may vary. Net Revenues are Gross Revenues net of Royalty Fees, Marketing Contributions, Technology Fees and Promissory Note payments. The franchisee must establish electronic funds transfer and sign the ACH authorization; premiums, policy fees and agency fees received directly must be forwarded within 24 hours; the franchisor pays Net Revenues on the 25th day of each Month; overdue payments bear 18% per annum, and amounts the franchisor pays on the franchisee's behalf bear interest at 2% per Month or the maximum lawful rate.

entry.value: Written notice of termination at least 30 days before the effective date of termination (10 days for any failure to pay the Initial Franchise Fee or an installment, or any failure to timely enter information into the agency management system), with an opportunity to cure within that period or such longer period as applicable law may require; the events in Section 17.1 automatically terminate all rights without notice, and the events in Section 17.2 terminate effective immediately upon written notice without any opportunity to cure. State amendments, effective only where their jurisdictional requirements are met, provide: the California amendment gives 60 days after receipt of written notice of default to remedy it; the Minnesota amendment requires 90 days' notice of termination (with 60 days to cure) and 180 days' notice of non-renewal.
